observations: A complete KV JSON object with a declared body ten bytes longer previously created a handle and reached an injection sink after equally truncated metadata. Fixed read, current and consume paths deny without retained handles or injection.

Exact encoded-byte Content-Length equality is required; duplicate, invalid or conflicting framing and exposed header-parser defects deny before body reads. Valid fixed, chunked and EOF-delimited responses remain distinct.

Negative chunk-size variants would cause the unguarded stdlib parser to call read(-1). The guarded response denies before any underlying body read; direct oversized internal requests also deny before read.
An independent buffer spy observes at most 65537 payload bytes through many chunks, plus separately counted chunk delimiters; oversized bodies deny before returning a Response.

Every normal or rejected HTTP path attempts both response and connection cleanup without retry. Real HTTPConnection detachment tests retain live exception tracebacks to prove files close; ordinary cleanup failures deny without handles, expose no canaries and do not mask a primary framing failure.
Canary scans cover formatted public exceptions, stdout and stderr. Independent sink-effect and underlying-byte-read observations detect deliberate framing and private-read guard mutations.

The SRC-006 manifest updates only the hash of the existing protocol test fixture to account for its HTTPMessage headers; original source coverage, provenance, pending acceptance and historical evidence records remain unchanged.
